question: Sanctions on the ICC: right call or wrong call?

lines.text: The United States has sanctioned the International Criminal Court itself.
lines.note: US State Department, 9 Oct 2026: the ICC is designated under E.O. 14203

lines.text: It came hours after a former ICC judge won the Nobel Peace Prize.
lines.note: Reuters and Irish Times: sanctions hours after Navi Pillay won the Nobel

lines.text: The committee honoured Navi Pillay for promoting peace and international law.
lines.note: Norwegian Nobel Committee citation, 9 Oct 2026; Pillay was UN human rights chief 2008 to 2014

lines.text: Marco Rubio says America will ban transactions with the court.
lines.note: Rubio: 'We will ban transactions with this rogue court'

lines.text: His words: Either the ICC will end its threats, or we will end the ICC.

scene.quote: Either the ICC will end its threats, or we will end the ICC.
scene.who: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State

lines.text: The BBC says US firms can no longer give it services like banking or software.
lines.note: BBC: sanctions bar US companies from providing goods or services such as banking or software

lines.text: Rubio says Trump will never let the court prosecute Americans.
lines.note: Rubio: 'President Trump will never allow the International Criminal Court to prosecute Americans.'

lines.text: The BBC says the US also objects to its warrants for Israeli leaders, including Netanyahu.
lines.note: BBC: US anger over a closed Afghanistan probe and ICC warrants for Israeli officials including Netanyahu; Netanyahu welcomed the sanctions

lines.text: The court calls it an assault on the rule of law, and says it will not be deterred.
lines.note: ICC statement via BBC: 'an assault on the rule of law', 'will not be deterred'

lines.text: Britain, France, Germany, Japan and four other allies say they strongly disagree.
lines.note: GOV.UK joint statement: UK, Canada, Denmark, Germany, France, Italy, Japan, Netherlands

lines.text: The court has 125 member states. The United States has never joined.
lines.note: BBC and Modern Diplomacy: 125 member states; founded 2002

lines.text: Rubio warns the campaign to dismantle the court will go on, brick by brick.
lines.note: Rubio: 'the United States will continue its campaign to dismantle the ICC, brick by brick'

lines.text: Sanctions on the ICC: right call or wrong call?
